fatal_errors: The proposed sulfur-atmosphere heat treatment is not the target intervention, which was increasing Mo content in an already formulated Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
The assumed starting alloy lacks the pre-existing lubricants and oxide additives central to the target material.
The claimed broad-temperature action of MoS2 is unsupported and neglects its oxidation and loss of lubricity at elevated temperatures in air.
No prior evidence is cited despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses self-lubricating HEAs and proposes a genuinely falsifiable treated-versus-untreated tribology experiment, but it does not reconstruct the studied material or intervention. It replaces Mo-alloying and sigma-phase strengthening with sulfurization, omits Ag, Ni-coated MoS2, Cr2O3, lattice distortion, and high-temperature silver-molybdate/NiO glaze formation, and covers only approximately 25–600 °C rather than room temperature to 800 °C under the specified dry-sliding conditions. Its low-shear MoS2 mechanism has limited conceptual overlap with the low-temperature mechanism in the target, but cannot justify simultaneous friction and wear reductions throughout the proposed range. The generic untreated baseline, arbitrary 30–50% prediction, and absence of literature evidence make the alternative scientifically under-supported, although the proposed microscopy, diffraction, friction, and wear measurements could test it.
